instruction: Add a single-instance lock so a duplicate HOLLY launch exits and focuses the running window instead of contending for the profile's LevelDB locks.

notes: app.requestSingleInstanceLock() is placed immediately after app.setPath('userData', PROFILE_DIR) because the lock is keyed on userData; earlier placement would guard the default directory. Next: 096 wire main.js (must use dynamic await import() for the ESM vault core from CommonJS main.js), 098 vault window + Ctrl+Shift+K, 100 vendor built UI.

notes: Root cause: dispose() fires on win.on('closed') and removed all eight tab channel handlers, but the renderer is still tearing down and invokes tab:activate after that point, so Electron logged 'Error occurred in handler for tab:activate: No handler registered'. It was a late harmless call, not a missing feature - the handler is registered normally at tab-view-manager.js:359. Fix: dispose() now installs an answering stub ({ok:false, error:'tab views disposed'}) on each channel instead of leaving the channel bare. Because stubs would otherwise make a second window's ipcMain.handle throw 'second handler', the IPC surface now clears any stale handler for all eight channels before registering, via a single TAB_CHANNELS list used by both registration and dispose - previously the channel list was duplicated as a literal in dispose() only. instruction: Create the vault window: its own session, vault-preload.js attached, VAULT_WINDOW_ID pinned on creation and cleared on close, opened with Ctrl+Shift+K. This is the action that makes the vault reachable.
verification: agent-preflight PASS, clean tree at 22434fc before the change. npm run check -> CHECK-PASSED. npm run smoke -> [smoke] PASS, vault line present, no tab:activate error. Live end-to-end: launched HOLLY, focused a real browser tab on a web page, pressed Ctrl+Shift+K, and the Keychain window opened as a separate top-level window (confirmed via EnumWindows: 'Keychain - Password Manager' and 'HOLLY' both present as distinct visible windows). The vendored UI rendered correctly on its first-run screen with the locally-bundled Space Grotesk. Log shows '[Holly] Vault window open (webContents 3) - state: empty' with no preload error, no blocked-navigation warning, and nothing in stderr.
notes: Session isolation is the important decision here: the window uses session.fromPartition('persist:holly-vault'), NOT the browsing session persist:holly. Extensions are loaded into persist:holly, so a vault window sharing it would have Tampermonkey and Dark Reader injecting content scripts into the page displaying decrypted passwords. Hardening on the window: sandbox true, contextIsolation true, nodeIntegration false, webviewTag false, will-navigate refused and setWindowOpenHandler denying popups, so the window cannot be steered to a URL or phished. Closing the window locks the vault and clears VAULT_WINDOW_ID, so the IPC guard closes with it - leaving the key in memory with no window to lock from would be the worst of both. A 2s watcher sends vault:locked to the renderer only on a real unlocked->locked transition. Ctrl+Shift+K is registered per-webContents via before-input-event rather than globalShortcut, so it works from inside a tab but does not fire when HOLLY is not the focused application. Remaining known gap, not a defect in this action: the auto-lock preference is not persisted and resets to 15 minutes each launch, because HOLLY has no settings layer yet.

notes: Three small pieces: a row in the overflow menu markup (src/index.html, key glyph, tooltip naming the Ctrl+Shift+K shortcut), a click listener in src/renderer.js invoking holly:vault:open, and the handler in main.js. The overflow menu is rebuilt as a NATIVE popup by popupNativeMenu(), which reads the HTML rows and dispatches clicks back to each row's button, so no separate native-menu registration was needed. Channel naming matters: holly:vault:open sits OUTSIDE the guarded vault:* surface on purpose. The vault:* channels answer only the vault window; this one opens a window and returns nothing about the vault - not its state, not its entries, not whether one exists - so the chrome UI may safely call it. It refuses a call from the vault window itself. Web content cannot reach it regardless, having no preload and therefore no ipcRenderer. Next: autofill, which needs its own sandbox proof before any of it goes near main.js - a content script in a web page asking the vault questions deliberately punches a hole in the single-authorised-window model that everything so far rests on.
